test-release-package-dist: pin trace-reader TODOs 269 to 273 (#286)

Case 27 of tools/test-release-package-dist.py now holds the 5 gaps
that TODOs 269 to 273 record for the trace reader, each with a case
that fails without it. Its docstrings state a rule for what the
reader refuses, with examples, and point to the reader functions as
the code that makes its refusals. The packager and the reader are
unchanged.

- fork() = 101 is read as the call, and its child starts in the
  folder of its maker. A child of fork() = 101 or vfork() = 101 keeps
  that folder when its maker enters another by chdir after the call,
  also when strace left the call unfinished and resumed it with the
  id of the child at the next line, and when a line of the child
  interrupted the call and it is resumed with the id of the child.
- For each of clone, clone3, fork and vfork, in each of the 9 forms
  in which strace cuts a call short and when it ends with the result
  ? and the note <unavailable>, 1 later process with no maker is
  read by its absolute paths, and a second ends the case, as does a
  relative path in that process. The second ends it for each of
  these first calls of the first: a chdir or an fchdir whose result
  is 0, an unread call, a clone, clone3, fork or vfork that made a
  process, and an unlink, a chdir or a fork that failed. After 2, 3
  or 4 such calls of the same name in the same form, as many such
  processes are read and 1 more ends the case; after a fork and a
  vfork that each ended with the result ?, 2 are read and a third
  ends it.
- A new test checks that rule on generated traces: each order of at
  most 4 calls cut short, C, and 1 to 5 processes with no maker, N,
  in which only the last N may find no C left for it, with each of
  180 call attributes and 1 first call, and with each of 177 first
  calls and 1 call attribute; and 1 call and 2 processes with each
  pair of them. A call attribute is clone, clone3, fork or vfork, or
  clone or clone3 with CLONE_FS, in each of the 10 forms above, by a
  process whose folder is known, by 1 whose shared folder is not
  known or by a process with no maker. A first call is an unread
  call in each of the 9 forms, or a call of each name that the test
  asks strace for, or clone or clone3 with CLONE_FS, done, failed or
  in each of the 10 forms. All the C of a trace take 1 call
  attribute, and all its N 1 first call. A trace also holds such
  calls and processes that are not C or N: before each C by a
  process with no maker, a clone that strace detached from and the
  process with no maker that it lets start, which makes the C; and
  each N whose first call is such a call. So a trace holds up to 9
  such calls and up to 9 such processes, but in none of these traces
  does the rule leave more than 4 such calls untaken at the same
  time, and in none does a process make a call after its own call
  cut short. A reader that breaks the rule only in a trace that the
  test does not generate passes it, such as 1 that breaks it only
  while more than 4 such calls are untaken.
- A process with no maker ends the case after a clone, clone3, fork
  or vfork whose result is 0, and after an unread call of ??? or of
  each name that the test asks strace for but fork and vfork, clone(
  and clone3( among them, in each of the 9 forms.
- An unlink read with its arguments that ends as "= ? <unavailable>"
  counts as a removal, in its line and in its resumption. After a
  chdir that ends that way in a shared folder, an absolute path is
  read and a relative path ends the case with the error that names
  it. That strace writes this form for a call whose arguments it
  read is not verified, and the comment and the module docstring say
  so.
- fchdir into a descriptor with no path, or with a relative path,
  ends the case.
- renameat2 gives both of its paths, each read against its own
  descriptor, in a case where the 2 descriptors and the folder of
  the process name 3 different folders.
- New subtests hold refusals that no case on main held, among them
  those of a trace with no call, a resumption with no call open or
  under another name, a path not in hex escapes, a line with no
  process id, an unread call cut short while a call is open, a line
  with no space or with a tab after the process id, with a space or
  a tab before it, or whose process id has a sign, a call with no
  space before or after its = or with 2 spaces after it, a result in
  hexadecimal or with a plus sign, a result of ? with text right
  after it, with no space between them, a path in a string that
  strace cut short, or in a string with an octal escape, a letter
  escape or a hex escape of 1 digit, a descriptor whose path strace
  cut short, or 1 in hexadecimal, with a plus sign or written as
  at_fdcwd in small letters, a resumption with 2 spaces or with no
  space after <... or before resumed, a call, a call that strace
  detached from or a resumption whose name holds a capital letter,
  and a relative path in a thread that a clone or clone3 with
  CLONE_FS made while the folder of its maker was not known.
- The error of each raise statement of the reader functions is
  checked whole by 1 or more subtests, as is the error for a line of
  a process after each kind of call at which the reader finds that
  the process ended. Some refusals share the text of their error, so
  such a check does not show which of them ended the case: a
  resumption with no call open and 1 under another name; a call cut
  short and 1 that strace detached from while another call of its
  process is open; 3 refusals in trace_call of a call that the test
  cannot read; a line of a process after a call that strace
  detached from, 1 after an unread call left unfinished and 1 after
  an unread call that ended with the result ?; a relative path in a
  process with no maker, 1 in a folder that a chdir or fchdir that
  strace cut short left not known, 1 in a child that a process whose
  folder was not known made without CLONE_FS and 1 in a thread that
  such a process made with CLONE_FS, which shares that folder; and a
  process that no traced call made when no call cut short came
  before it and 1 when each such call has let 1 start. The
  docstrings say so. Each of these refusals is checked whole by 1 or
  more subtests, among them a relative path after a chdir or an
  fchdir that strace detached from or that ended with the result ?
  in a shared folder, 1 in a child that a clone, clone3, fork or
  vfork made without CLONE_FS in a process with no maker or after
  such a chdir or fchdir, and 1 in a thread that clone or clone3
  with CLONE_FS made in each of those 3 kinds of process.
- Among the examples of refusals in the module docstring are 2 for
  relative paths, not a list of all that end the case: 1 of a
  process with no maker, with no descriptor or with AT_FDCWD, in a
  removal whose result is 0, ? or not given, or in a chdir whose
  result is 0, before a chdir or fchdir whose result is 0 gives that
  process a folder; and 1 of any process, in such a removal, against
  a descriptor whose path strace -y does not give, gives as relative
  or gives as that of a removed folder. Subtests hold both at each
  path of each removal, both paths of rename, renameat and renameat2
  among them, with the result 0 and in each of the 10 forms: the
  first at each path with no descriptor or against AT_FDCWD, and the
  second at each path of unlinkat, renameat and renameat2 in the
  first process, in a process that a call made and in a process
  with no maker; and they hold the chdir. Another ends the case at a
  rename with 1 argument with an IndexError, the error that the
  module docstring gives as an example of another error. The module
  docstring states the rule of the new test and points to its
  docstring, which states the traces that it checks. The module
  docstring and the docstring of the folder test state that a
  relative path is read against the folder that its descriptor
  names, but against the folder of its process for AT_FDCWD, and
  subtests of the folder test hold this at each path of each
  removal.
- The test derives each path of each removal, and the descriptor
  that it is read against, from the arguments of the call as its
  manual page names them, not from the reader's table of removals,
  which a mutant of the reader may change. A subtest of the refusal
  test and 1 of the folder test fail if a name of that table, a path
  that it gives or a descriptor form of that path has no subtest.
  Each takes the forms and the kinds of process that it wants from
  lists of its own, not from the tables that write the subtests, so
  that an entry dropped from such a table fails it; the refusal test
  takes the results from a list that names each form, not from the
  tables of forms that write its subtests.
- Each subtest whose trace resumes a call with the result ? says
  "resumed with ?" in its label.

Checks: python3 -I tools/test-release-package-dist.py TraceReaderTests
is expected to give 5 tests, OK, here and 3 tests, OK, on main. Each
of the 91 reader mutants that the pull request description lists is
expected to pass case 27 on main, and each but cap-4 and
allowance-from-fifth, which break the rule only while more than 4
such calls are untaken, to fail it here. In a git checkout with
strace, the full run is expected to leave cases 1 to 26 as they are
on main.
